name: Summit of E-Wrestling Update

date.source: The Google Groups viewer's own timestamp on the post, 14 June 1991.

notes: The Summit's own first pre-event broadcast, four weeks out. It stages no match of its own — it announces the dates and the three-federation field, names the first five signed bouts, prints the battle royal's entry list and the tag tournament's field against the federation each entrant was to represent, and carries six taped promos. Recorded as a show because it is one of the institution's own broadcasts; its own text is where the first Summit's shape is set out, and no result belongs to it.

name: Summit of E-Wrestling Update #2

date.source: The Google Groups viewer's own timestamp on the post, 7 July 1991.

notes: The second and last pre-event broadcast, three days out. It runs the whole opening card match by match, prints the sixteen-team tag tournament bracket with its seedings, and stages two qualifying matches of its own for the last two places in that bracket — the earliest Summit matches this collection holds.

matches.note: Prof. Wolfman pinned Baron Von Klaw after Missy Holliday distracted him out of the Klaw Hold and Wolfman came off the top rope with a bone pulled out of his own leathers. The Academics took one of the sixteen tournament places.

Sargent Glasnost and Tomahawk hit the Hammer and Sickle and Michael kicked out of it; Annie came in, threw Glasnost over the top rope and beat Tomahawk with the Missionary Man crucifix. The Androgynes took the last tournament place.

name: The Summit of E-Wrestling, Card #1

date.source: The Google Groups viewer's own timestamp on the post, 10 July 1991; the broadcast itself is billed live from the Rosemont Horizon that night.

notes: The first night of the first Summit. Eleven matches with wrestlers from three federations on them, four of those matches for a member federation's own championship, called by the WeWF's own announce team with the PWGeA's ring announcer on introductions and the EMWA's security chief posted at ringside. One title changed hands: the Aztec Mummy took the PWGeA North American Championship off Mr. Mercury in a lumberjack match. The main event, the WeWF and PWGeA World Champions against each other with both belts on the line, went to a double count-out.

matches.note: The Mage's Gallery of the EMWA against the WeWF's Four Corners and the PWGeA's Shadow Assassins. Metallicus was the sole survivor.
A slingshot suplex, after Jack Moran's cane. Cogburn choked the Reaper with a hangman's noose afterwards until Bruno Morales's security force drove him off.
Bjorn retained: an elbow drop off the ropes after Smooth grabbed his tights to break up a monkey flip. Lightning Bolt had reversed the Sweedish Pretzel figure four earlier in the match.

Signed after Plague Dog interfered in a General-versus-Animal singles match. Sledge Hammer finally completed the backslide on Plague Dog as the General clotheslined him. Dr. Down-Under TASER'd Sledge Hammer twice afterwards and the Hoosiers ran in to break it up.

PWGeA North America Title. TITLE CHANGE: the Aztec Mummy pinned Mr. Mercury after a fireball, the Mummy's Claw and a splash, and became North American Champion — the only title to change hands on the first Summit. Twenty lumberjacks surrounded the ring and several of them took turns on the champion outside it.
Katrina hooked her legs under Molly Maguire's shoulders on an attempted body slam and rolled forward into the pin. Both wrestlers shook hands afterwards.

The Hoosiers retained with the Hoosier Homecoming. Erik slammed Robby the Lame's face into the commentary table on the way to the ring and the Hoosiers later double-suplexed him onto Panther; Lord Winfred Vague called the rest of the match in his place.
Admiral Chekov's team against Emperor Lightfinger's. The Romulan Mauler beat the count back in and Darth Vader did not.

PWGeA Tag Team Titles. Club Anarchy retained: Dr. Lethe fell head first to the floor after Oroboros ran in and made Judge Anderson let go of his foot. Silvah Hypocrisy kissed Judge Anderson mid-match and left him walking in circles, then kissed Baboon Tempest, who spent the next two matches barking.

A small package, after Tom "The Animal" Brown spat in Mr. B's face and the Black Knight's blindside hit Brown instead. Dr. Down-Under TASER'd his own wrestler after the bell and the 007 Special broke up.

matches.stipulation: WeWF and PWGeA World Titles, title for title
matches.note: The first Summit's main event, and the only match on either Summit with two World Championships on the line at once. Both men were counted out brawling on the floor; no belt changed hands. Thunder hit Flint with the PWGeA belt afterwards while offering a handshake.

Five interview segments open it. Fury won it, and was assaulted in his own celebration by five men who put him out of the following night's tournament and out of wrestling for two months.

matches.note: Wrestlers entered one at a time for the first ten and two at a time thereafter. Fury of the Mage's Gallery won it, last eliminating Bjorn "The Sweedish Pretzel", who could not stop his own charge when Fury pulled his arms free of the ropes. The Romulan Mauler scored the most eliminations; the Tholian Black Widow placed third. The new PWGeA North American Champion lasted four seconds.

name: The Summit of E-Wrestling, Card #3: the Road Warrior's Cup

date.source: The Google Groups viewer's own timestamp on the post, 12 July 1991.

notes: The third and last night of the first Summit: the Road Warrior's Cup, a sixteen-team single-elimination tag tournament in front of a billed 67,000. Eight first-round matches are recapped from tape and the seven that follow are called live. All three member federations' own tag-team champions entered it and none of them reached the final; the Soviets, who held nothing, won it.

matches.note: Won by count-out: the Wizard threw Annie over the top rope after the Hunter had DDT'd her on the concrete, and the count reached ten.
The night's first upset. Jake Shield held Angus Campbell at arm's length for the Shieldbearer smash; Panther slipped the grip and Campbell knocked out his own partner, and Panther covered him.
Frank Steel piledrove Peregrine Falcon, who had already beaten a count of ten after landing head first on the astroturf.

Won by count-out. Revenge of the Nerds were a last-minute replacement for the 007 Special, who had broken up two nights earlier; CALTECH produced a test tube of synthetic green mist and both members of Double Trouble were counted out.

The Ultimate Trekkies beat the reigning PWGeA World Tag Team Champions: the Black Widow slid out of a body slam and rolled Captain Necropolis up from behind. Admiral Chekov spewed Silvah Hypocrisy in the face before the match and the BattleCruisers tarred and feathered her during it.
Maniac #2 gorilla-pressed Prof. Wolfman and clotheslined him on the top rope for the fall while the referee was breaking up a fight between Prof. Spewmaster and Simon Bolendorf outside the ring.

The longest match of the tournament: Erik pinned Photon Torpedo with a bridged back-to-back suplex at 29:53 of a thirty-minute time limit, seven seconds from a draw that would have eliminated both teams.

The Magician threw in the towel: Warren Hammer had wrestled with cuts from the previous night's assault and was bleeding from the nose and forehead. Fury, the Rumble winner, had already been ruled out for two months with five broken ribs and a broken leg.
The Soviets eliminated the top seeds: Bear blocked a double underhook suplex, backdropped the Wizard and bridged over him. The Hunter had thrown the Zampolit into the third row earlier in the match.
Seventeen seconds: Frank Steel power-slammed CALTECH and pinned him. The ring announcer read the time out.
Erik, bleeding and worked over for most of the match, caught Ford Firepower with a flying cross body block off the second rope. Both teams shook hands afterwards.

Won by disqualification: Jimmy Vendetta, Randy Hurricane and Club Anarchy came down the aisle and Captain Necropolis hit the Black Widow with a chair, and the referee disqualified the Maniacs for it. The commentary desk noted that Simon Bolendorf looked as surprised as anyone.
Panther locked his legs round Frank Steel's head out of a piledriver and rolled him over. The Zampolit had knocked Mike Flint out with his cane on the floor.
The Romulan Mauler power-bombed Erik. The commentary desk called it the Hoosiers' first loss as a team.

The Soviets won the first Road Warrior's Cup: Bear declined a piledriver his own back could no longer take and gave the Romulan Mauler a gourdbuster instead. Between them the two finalists had beaten all three of the member federations' reigning tag-team champions on the way.

name: The Summit of E-Wrestling, Day 1

date.source: The Google Groups viewer's own timestamp on the post, 27 December 1991.

notes: The opening night of the second Summit, billed by its own host as a week-long event pitting the best of the WeWF, the UeWF, the UFWS and the IWF against each other — four federations where the first Summit had three. Two venues in one broadcast: an eight-man tag from the Montreal Forum, then the UeWF's own inaugural championship tournaments from Madison Square Garden. The World Championship tournament's first round is given as a bare results list, held earlier the same day; its second round is called match by match. The document's own printed second-round bracket does not agree with its own first-round results — it lists Brimstone Baxter against "Fabulous" Eddie Awesome, and then stages Lord Plunder, who had beaten Baxter, against Awesome instead. The staged match is what is structured here and the discrepancy is left standing.

name: The Summit of E-Wrestling, Day 2

date.source: The Google Groups viewer's own timestamp on the post, 28 December 1991.

notes: The second night of the second Summit, and the night three of the UeWF's own first championships were settled. Both semi-finals of that federation's World Championship tournament were announced in advance as double-purpose matches: the loser of the first was to be named its first Atlantic Champion, the loser of the second its first Pacific Champion. Between them, an eight-woman battle royal crowned its first Ladies Champion. The card closes with a forty-man Royal Rumble for a trophy, its whole field read out by name and federation before the bell.

matches.note: Won by disqualification: the referee found the roll of quarters Admiral Ax had punched Mr. B with. The Armed Forces had attacked Mr. B's party before the bell, which the commentary desk pointed out could not be a disqualification because the match had not started. Announced beforehand as crowning a champion either way — the loser was to be named the UeWF's first Atlantic Champion, and Admiral Ax was.

name: The Summit of E-Wrestling, Day 3

date.source: The Google Groups viewer's own timestamp on the post, 29 December 1991.

appearances.note: At ringside with Da Boyz for the Von Erich/Freebird Memorial tournament — “They will be facing Da Boyz, Guido and Nunzio of the WeWF”, with Da Boss in their corner. The appearance the strong-joins pass of 2026-09-02 found in no wing's row.

notes: The densest card the Summit ever ran: seventeen matches in one night, fourteen of them the first Von Erich/Freebird Memorial six-man tag tournament. Fourteen trios entered it, two of them seeded straight into the second round; two of the four second-round matches ended without a winner advancing, so the semi-final round ran with three teams and a bye. Before the tournament, two managers wrestled each other and the Klingons beat the UeWF's own top-ranked tag team.

matches.note: A manager against a manager, and the second Summit's answer to a grudge that had started when Chekov's Klingons took the WeWF tag titles off Bolendorf's Maniacs. Both men were counted out brawling on the floor with their own wrestlers piling in around them; it took several referees to break it up.
The Klinshai Bombing, a double flying headbutt off the top rope, Klingon Phaser pinning Rage. The Dangerous Emotions were the UeWF's own number-one ranked tag team at the time.

name: The Summit of E-Wrestling, Day 4

date.source: The Google Groups viewer's own timestamp on the post, 30 December 1991.

notes: The fourth night, and the last of the second Summit this collection holds. Four matches: the second round of the UeWF's own tag-team tournament, a WeWF tag match, the crowning of an Ultimate Heavyweight Champion in front of a table of four federation presidents, and a name match between two wrestlers billed under the same ring name in two different federations, the loser to give it up. The broadcast closes by advertising a fifth night — the UeWF tag final, an Iron Lady tournament for ladies' tag champions, and a Slick Ric trophy tournament — that no document in the held record carries.

matches.stipulation: UeWF World Tag Team Championship tournament, second round
matches.note: Two trips through the Veg-O-Matic on Burn, with Crash's knee already clipped by a chair and Lord Plunder bulldogged out on the floor. The Dangerous Emotions went into a final against the Armed Forces that no held document carries.
Erik power-slammed Rusty Nose. Baboon Tempest was in the Hoosiers' corner and hit Rusty with a chair during the match; he came back with another one afterwards and Rustin pulled his father clear.

The first Ultimate Heavyweight Champion. The belt was made for a challenge between the only two men in e-wrestling then holding major titles in two federations at once; by the time the match happened both had lost those belts, and the four federation presidents at ringside let the match stand anyway. Ace Diamond hit Cogburn with the belt after the Bulldog Supreme, Cogburn fell on top of Steelgrave, and the referee counted the pin.

Two wrestlers billed under the same ring name in two different federations, with the name itself at stake. The commentary desk called them the Good Sandman and the Bad SandMan on air because it could not otherwise tell readers them apart. The WeWF's Sandman won it with a bulldog and the UFWS's SandMan was told from the desk to find a new moniker.

name: The Seventh Summit's Road Warrior Tournament

date.source: The Google Groups viewer's own timestamp on the post, 23 June 1995. The broadcast itself opens mid-tournament and its writer records that it is six months late; the tournament it finishes was staged earlier and the date here is the date the record enters the archive, not the date the card was held.

notes: Four years after the first Summit, the seventh Summit's own Road Warrior tournament, written up and posted six months late by a hand that had held the results all along. The play-by-play breaks off before the final, which its writer summarises in his own voice rather than leave unwritten. Two ring names from the first Summit's opening night are on it, billed out of a federation that did not exist in 1991 and introduced as the Original Shadow Assassins. Its closing line names the institution by what it had grown into: any of the fine Summit Alliance federations.

matches.note: Zombie's Death Drop Powerbomb on the Good Knight, who had let a Boston crab go to stare at a man in the crowd the commentary desk thought might be King Midnight.

Won by count-out, ruled on the replay: the officiating referee had gone down, an official called the Wall counted both teams out, and the tape showed Ice Trey had beaten the count while his partner was hitting people with a chair.
Steve Stuart rolled up Johnny Vicious, who had been blinded by the flashlight Mayhem's manager was carrying. A cream pie and a bottle of seltzer water had already gone into the match.

Death Warmed Over won the seventh Summit's Road Warrior tournament: DWO's Burial, a slingshot into a Zombie DDT, on Ron Kukelbauer. Their semi-final never happened — the MIW's own commissioner announced on behalf of the Summit's officials that both teams from the other quarter-final had been hospitalised after a locker-room fight and that Death Warmed Over had a bye into the final. The writer's own note breaks the play-by-play off here and summarises the match instead.
